title: Don't outsource the best parts of parenting to AI
excerpt: Talking to your kids is one of the fun parts of parenting. I'd rather AI take over mundane tasks like laundry or organizing school communications.
content_html:
By Katie Notopoulos

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Senior Correspondent covering technology and culture

There are a lot of things about parenting that are unpleasant drudgery. There's the obvious ones: diapers, cleaning bottle parts, picking up Legos, listening to "Wheels on the Bus" over and over.

As kids get older, you'll also discover so many more annoying things: The constant sorting of too-small clothes, dividing between storage, donation, and hand-me-downs. All the separate apps for messaging used by schools, bus companies, daycares, and sports leagues seem to have UI designed by Satan himself. The fact that there will be at least one early release or day off from school on a random non-holiday day you learn about the day before. And the most grueling scourge of it all: summer camp signup.

I embrace the idea of ceding some of the unfun mental load of parenting to AI.

That's different than delegating away the parts of parenting that, sure, take time and effort and being present — but are also the precious interactions you'll miss when your kids are grown up.

AI can help parents, but how is key

I would love a robot that could fold laundry. It does seem like the separate messaging app problem should be solvable (I pray for the singularity whenever I get a push notification from the dedicated school messaging app about a new message containing Google Drive link to the PDF that lists all the daily themes for school spirit week).

Sure, great! But there are also some clunker ideas of what you could use AI for with parenting.

cool use case of chatgpt work i heard last night:

connect your family calendars and explain your kids' interests.

every morning for the drive to school, have it make a podcast that talks about one kid's soccer game that afternoon, one kid's upcoming birthday, some news, etc.

— Sam Altman (@sama) July 31, 2026

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, a parent himself, recently posted to X about what he described as a cool use for AI: making a custom podcast for kids about their interests and calendar to listen to during their drive to school. The backlash was swift, the main response being something along the lines of, "What if you just talked to your children?"

I agree with that critique, for the most part. And more so: why would I want to give up that actually pleasant task?

Sure, I think an audio reminder of that day/week's afterschool activities is probably helpful for kids. Keeping on top of the calendar does get difficult when kids get older and busier, especially if there are multiple kids.

This is something where a technological solution feels within our grasp. Something like Skylight's "smart family calendar" or AI chatbot apps that act as personal assistants for busy parents.

My colleague Ben Shimkus talked to a Ford exec who vibecoded family "chief of staff" that sends a daily email to her and her husband going over the calendar of daycare drop-offs, appointments, activities, and other kid-related items for the day.

Dealing with the gruntwork of managing a calendar is something many parents would be happy to offload to AI or some other tech to deal with. I'm less confident in Altman's idea of making this a whole "podcast" instead of just a brief audio calendar reminder. I suspect my elementary-aged kids would find this cringe and annoying.

But I see why so many people reacted so strongly to his tweet. It's suggesting more than just an automated calendar reminder — it's taking the place of time that could otherwise be spent talking to your kids.

Talking to your kids is the fun part

Talking to your kids about their upcoming soccer game or birthday is one of the enjoyable, pleasurable experiences of parenting. Those nice moments of positive connection, chatting in the car, are something I suspect most parents aren't looking to give up or outsource.

This is one of the overall challenges with where we are with AI right now: AI might be capable of doing some of the tasks we find pleasurable and enjoyable (like creative writing or drawing), but what many people want is for it to take on the ones we don't want to do.

Meta is testing out an app called Storykit that allows parents to create AI-generated bedtime stories for kids. "Write a story about a teddy bear in a magical forest" is a task that an LLM is very capable of doing, and there is probably some fun novelty for kids to have a personalized story — the kids might enjoy it a few times.

I'd argue that making up stories at bedtime for your kids is one of those rewarding parts of parenting you shouldn't outsource. Though it may sometimes feel like there are 3,000 minutes between 7 and 8 p.m., the reality is that the years your kids want to hear you make up stories at bedtime is shockingly brief.

These are the sweet moments people dream of when they want to become parents: making up stories at bedtime, or peering at your kids in the rearview mirror while chatting about soccer games and birthday gift wish lists. These moments are the reward for putting up with all the grinding drudgery or the endless put-on-your-shoes reminders.

There are plenty of annoying and mundane parts of dealing with young kids — any parent could help you identify those tasks. Those things are often hard for AI to take over (good news to the parent in charge of emptying the Diaper Genie: your job is safe from AI).

The things that are fun and pleasant might be easier for AI to replicate — but who wants that?

content_html_zh:
作者：Katie Notopoulos 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。 资深记者报道科技与文化

养育子女有很多事情是令人不愉快的苦差事。 有一些显而易见的事情：尿布、清洁瓶子零件、捡起乐高积木、一遍又一遍地听“巴士上的轮子”。

随着孩子年龄的增长，你还会发现更多烦人的事情：不断地对太小的衣服进行分类，划分存储、捐赠和旧衣服。 学校、公交公司、日托中心和体育联盟使用的所有单独的消息传递应用程序似乎都有撒旦本人设计的用户界面。 事实上，您在前一天了解到，在随机的非假期日，至少会有一次提早放学或放假一天。 其中最令人痛苦的祸害是：夏令营报名。

我接受将养育子女的一些无趣的精神负担交给人工智能的想法。

这与将养育孩子的部分委托给他人不同，这些部分当然需要时间、精力和在场，但也是孩子长大后你会怀念的宝贵互动。

AI可以帮助父母，但如何帮助才是关键

我想要一个可以叠衣服的机器人。 看来单独的消息应用程序问题应该是可以解决的（每当我从专门的学校消息应用程序收到关于一条新消息的推送通知时，我都会祈祷奇点，其中包含 Google Drive 链接到 PDF，其中列出了学校精神周的所有每日主题）。

当然，太棒了！ 但对于人工智能在育儿方面的用途，也存在一些笨拙的想法。

我昨晚听到的 chatgpt 工作的一个很酷的用例：连接您的家庭日历并解释您孩子的兴趣。每天早上开车去学校时，让它制作一个播客，谈论一个孩子当天下午的足球比赛、一个孩子即将到来的生日、一些新闻等。— Sam Altman (@sama) 2026 年 7 月 31 日

OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman（本人也是一位家长）最近在 X 上发布了他所描述的人工智能的一个很酷的用途：为孩子们制作一个关于他们的兴趣和日历的定制播客，供他们在开车上学时收听。 强烈的反对意见很快就出现了，主要的反应是“如果你只和你的孩子说话怎么办？”

我在很大程度上同意这种批评。 更重要的是：我为什么要放弃这项实际上令人愉快的任务？

当然，我认为当天/一周的课后活动的音频提醒可能对孩子们有帮助。 当孩子长大、变得更加忙碌时，尤其是在有多个孩子的情况下，掌握日历确实会变得困难。

这是我们感觉技术解决方案触手可及的事情。 像 Skylight 的“智能家庭日历”或人工智能聊天机器人应用程序一样，可以充当忙碌父母的私人助理。

我的同事本·希姆库斯（Ben Shimkus）与一位福特高管进行了交谈，她对家庭“幕僚长”进行了振动编码，每天向她和她的丈夫发送一封电子邮件，查看当天的日托接送、预约、活动和其他与孩子相关的项目的日历。

许多家长乐意将管理日历的繁琐工作交给人工智能或其他技术来处理。 我对奥特曼将其制作为一个完整的“播客”而不仅仅是一个简短的音频日历提醒的想法不太有信心。 我怀疑我的小学生会觉得这种畏缩和烦人。

但我明白为什么这么多人对他的推文反应如此强烈。 它不仅仅意味着自动日历提醒——它还取代了原本可以用来与孩子交谈的时间。

与孩子交谈是有趣的部分

与您的孩子谈论他们即将到来的足球比赛或生日是育儿过程中令人愉快的经历之一。 我怀疑大多数父母都不会放弃或外包那些积极联系的美好时刻，比如在车里聊天。

这是我们目前人工智能面临的总体挑战之一：人工智能可能能够完成一些我们觉得愉快和愉快的任务（例如创意写作或绘画），但许多人想要的是它承担我们不想做的任务。

Meta 正在测试一款名为 Storykit 的应用程序，该应用程序允许父母为孩子创建人工智能生成的睡前故事。 “写一个关于魔法森林里的泰迪熊的故事”是法学硕士非常有能力完成的任务，而且对于孩子们来说，拥有一个个性化的故事可能会有一些有趣的新奇——孩子们可能会喜欢几次。

我认为，在睡前为你的孩子编故事是你不应该外包的育儿过程中最有价值的部分之一。 尽管有时感觉晚上 7 点到 8 点之间只有 3,000 分钟，但事实上，孩子想听你在睡前编故事的时间却短得惊人。

当人们想成为父母时，这些都是他们梦想的甜蜜时刻：在睡前编故事，或者一边看着后视镜里的孩子，一边谈论足球比赛和生日礼物愿望清单。 这些时刻是对忍受所有苦差事或无休止的穿鞋提醒的奖励。

与年幼的孩子打交道有很多烦人且平凡的部分——任何父母都可以帮助你识别这些任务。 这些事情通常很难让人工智能接管（对于负责清空尿布精灵的家长来说，这是个好消息：你的工作不会受到人工智能的影响）。

有趣和令人愉快的事情可能更容易被人工智能复制——但谁想要这样呢？
